information_for_contributors: The word-list halves of this grammar (the keyword, primitive-type, attribute-marker and operator lists) are GENERATED from the compiler's exported tables by crates/vilan-cli/tests/grammar_sync.rs, which byte-gates them on every suite run. Do not hand-edit a generated `match`/`begin` value; change the compiler table (or grammar_sync.rs's role tables) and regenerate:
VILAN_REGENERATE_GRAMMARS=1 cargo test -p vilan-cli --test grammar_sync generated
The structural rules (strings, number shapes, elements, `css` blocks, captures, the contextual `context`/`sync` anchors) are hand-written.
name: Vilan

patterns.comment: Interpolated triple-quoted string `i"""...{expr}..."""` (H7) — the triple-quoted form with holes: RAW but for the two brace escapes `\{` and `\}`. First of all the string rules: the triple rule below does not match at the `i`, and the `i"` rule would end at the very next quote (the second of the three).
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.vilan

patterns.comment: Exactly two escapes exist here; a backslash before anything else is a literal backslash.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.vilan

patterns.comment: An interpolation hole. Its end also stops (without consuming) at a `"""`, so a hole can never swallow the closing delimiter — an unclosed `{` while typing corrupts at most the rest of the literal. A lone `"` is ordinary content here, so — unlike the single-quoted form — the hole does not stop at one.
patterns.name: meta.template.expression.vilan

patterns.comment: Triple-quoted string `"""..."""` — RAW and multi-line: no escapes, no interpolation; content runs to the first `"""`. Must be tried before the plain rule, or `"""` reads as an empty string plus a quote.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.vilan

patterns.comment: Interpolated string `i"...{expr}..."` — ONLY `i"` strings have holes; a `{` in a plain string is literal. `\b` keeps a trailing `i` of an identifier (`hi".."`) from reading as the prefix.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.vilan

patterns.comment: An interpolation hole. Its end also stops (without consuming) at a `"`, so a hole can never swallow the string's closing quote — an unclosed `{` while typing corrupts at most its own line. The trade: a string literal NESTED in a hole ends the hole early; rare, and the damage stays local.
patterns.name: meta.template.expression.vilan

patterns.comment: Plain string — `{`/`}` are literal characters, never interpolation.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.vilan

patterns.comment: Hex literal with an optional type suffix (`0xFF`, `0x80000000u32`, `0xDEADn`) — before the decimal rule, like the lexer.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.hex.vilan

patterns.comment: Decimal literal with an optional type suffix (`42u32`, `3.5f`, `0n`). The suffix admits digits after its first letter — `[A-Za-z_]*` alone can never satisfy the trailing `\b` inside `u32`, which left every digit-bearing suffix uncolored.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.vilan

patterns.comment: Bracket attributes: the built-in markers anywhere, plus GENERIC macro attributes `[name]` / `[name(args)]` at the start of a line (an expression's list literal never opens an item line, which keeps `[1, 2]` and `[x]` out).
patterns.name: meta.attribute.vilan

patterns.comment: The form words and the `retains` flag inside `[extern(..)]`.
patterns.name: support.constant.attribute.vilan

patterns.comment: A macro name — the attribute itself, or a lowercase derive name like `[derive(derive_display)]` (capitalized ones color as types above).
patterns.name: entity.name.function.macro.vilan

patterns.comment: `macro fun name` — a macro definition (macro-engine.md §3).
`macro name(..)` — a macro invocation (splice site).
`fun name` — the name in a function/method declaration.
Declaration keywords that introduce a named item.
patterns.name: storage.type.vilan

patterns.comment: `with` (trait impl / bound), the `borrows` return clause, and `css` (the head of a `css { … }` block).
patterns.name: keyword.other.vilan

patterns.comment: The `context` CLAUSE on a closure type — `(|| void) context owner_scope`, multi `context (a, b)`. It is a contextual keyword (a value or module may be NAMED `context`), and the clause only ever follows a parenthesized closure type — so the guard is: keyword only right after a `)`.

The `sync` MARKER on a closure type — `(sync || View) context owner_scope`. Contextual like `context` above (a bare `sync` is a type name), and it only ever opens a parenthesized closure type — so the guard is: keyword only right after a `(`.
Primitive types.
patterns.name: support.type.primitive.vilan

patterns.comment: User types / variants — PascalCase identifiers (and `Self`).
patterns.name: entity.name.type.vilan

patterns.comment: A lowercase identifier immediately followed by `(` is a call.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.vilan

patterns.comment: GENERATED value: the lexer's fused pairs (lexing.rs TWO_CHARACTER_OPERATORS), then the presentation-only sequences the parser reassembles (`&mut`, `<=`, `>=`, `?.` — grammar_sync.rs TEXTMATE_OPERATOR_EXTRAS), then single-char (incl. `^` bitwise-xor and postfix `?`/`!`).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.vilan

patterns.comment: Element syntax (element-syntax S2): a tag name glued to `<` or `</` — the grammar's own atom-position rule; a spaced comparison never matches.

A multi-line element head's terminator (E115). The rule above is a `match`, and a TextMate `match` sees one line at a time — so when a head's attributes are written one per line and the `>` lands on a line of its own, that rule cannot reach it and the operator list painted it as a comparison. A `>` or `/>` alone on its line is that terminator: the formatter breaks AFTER a binary operator and never before one, so no formatted line begins with a bare `>`. The language server paints the same bracket from the parse, which is the authority whenever it is running; this is what the file looks like without it.
The event form `on:click(…)`.
A hyphenated attribute name in a head (`aria-label(`, `data-id(`).
patterns.name: entity.other.attribute-name.vilan

patterns.comment: The `css { … }` block (css-block S4). Scoped as begin/end so that a property name is coloured as one only INSIDE a block — the entry is the grammar's own two-token gate, the keyword glued to `{`. Everything inside is `#css-items`; the block's own `}` is whatever `}` those patterns did not consume, which is why the hole and nested-rule rules below both take their braces with them.

A condition rule `.hover { … }` / `.within("data-theme", "dark") { … }`. The dot is the grammar's whole disambiguator, so a dotted head is a combinator and never a property. The head's arguments are taken in the `begin` rather than left to a nested rule, so the body's `{` is consumed here and the rule's own `}` closes it; a head whose arguments wrap across lines simply does not match, which is the regex level's honest limit.
A property name and its `:` — the span-adjacent name-`-`-name run the grammar reads, custom properties (`--brand-ink`) and vendor prefixes (`-webkit-…`) included.
A `{expression}` hole. Nested rules are matched first and take their own braces, so a bare `{` inside a block is always a hole; its contents are ordinary vilan.
The declaration terminator, which the grammar requires after every declaration including the last.
patterns.name: punctuation.terminator.vilan
